models.name: Universal four-step model (regional settings)
models.summary: One baseline engine everywhere · 382/382 US metros + 3,143 counties · census, travel-survey, OSM + transit data
models.description: The Julia four-step model: Generation (workers x rate) -> Distribution (gravity + IPF/Furness) -> Mode choice (share x calib / logit) -> Assignment (per-corridor BPR). Two calibration knobs (beta, transit_calib) solved by bisection per city. POLICY: this is ONE universal baseline — the same Julia engine runs every place — with REGIONAL SETTINGS per city (calibrated beta + transit share against sourced local targets) and settlement-type awareness: urban, rural, and suburban are calibrated as distinct travel-behavior contexts (suburban is deliberately not lumped into either).
models.coverage: 382/382 US metros + 3,143 counties; focused: Boston (TAZ · BG · tract · hex), Chicago, Seattle; intl 9 countries wired
models.data_in: workers, OD structure, transit utility, road network, ACS transit target, NHTS trip-length target
models.data_out: trips, transit_pct, avg_trip_mi, link flows / V-C, per-year 2010..2050
models.calibration: β bisected to NHTS 2017 trip length (11.06 vs 11.0 mi) · transit share to ACS B08301 (16.9% vs 17.1%) — per city · solver selectable per run: bisection (default) · IPF/Furness · Bayesian optimization — each documented in Methods

models.name: Transit-network centrality (Korea)
models.summary: BUILT (Seoul): ranks 471 real subway stations by degree/betweenness/closeness/PageRank on the OSM network — critical transfer hubs surface. See Outputs.
models.description: Builds a graph where nodes are subway stations and bus stops and edges are the route segments + walkable transfers between them, then computes classic network-centrality measures. Betweenness surfaces critical transfer hubs (removing them fractures journeys); degree = raw connectivity; closeness = how central a stop is to the whole network; PageRank/eigenvector = importance weighted by neighbours' importance. Output is a ranked list + a point/heat map of hub importance across Korea.
models.coverage: Korea — Seoul metro (subway + bus) first; extendable to Busan and the national bus/subway network as feeds allow.
models.cal_method: exact graph algorithms — no calibration constants; validated against known hub structure (e.g. Seoul's major interchange stations rank top).
models.calibration: n/a (deterministic); sanity check = major interchanges (Sadang, Gangnam, Jamsil, Seoul Stn) surface as high-betweenness hubs.
models.sources: Korea transit open data — data.go.kr TAGO (national bus/subway, free service key) · Seoul Open Data Plaza (data.seoul.go.kr) · GTFS via Mobility Database where published · OSM Korea (keyless network geometry + transfers).
models.standard: Freeman centrality (degree/closeness/betweenness) + PageRank/eigenvector; transit-graph construction per Derrible & Kennedy (network science of transit).
models.data_status: BUILT for Seoul: 471 stations from OpenStreetMap (keyless), 4 centralities computed. Top hubs match known interchanges (Express Bus Terminal, Jongno 3-ga). Bus + national + real ridership weights = the key-gated extension.
models.uses_model: Data foundation (network geometry) + Transit router (shared GTFS graph build)
models.provider: reproducible script — networkx over live OSM (keyless)
models.data_in: Korea GTFS/stops (subway stations + bus stops + route segments) · walkable-transfer links (OSM) · optional ridership weights.
models.data_out: Per-station degree/betweenness/closeness/PageRank + ranked hubs — VIEWABLE on the Outputs screen (471 real Seoul stations).

models.name: Travel-time heatmap (Korea, from an origin)
models.summary: BUILT (Seoul): estimated travel time from Seoul Station to all 471 stations — network model (33 km/h). See Outputs.
models.description: Single-source travel-time surface: from a chosen origin (and departure time), route to every destination zone using timetable-exact transit (RAPTOR) stitched with walk/road access, then interpolate the point times into a smooth surface with honest isochrone bands (15/30/45/60 min). This is the router's engine aimed FROM one origin TO all of Korea, rather than the fixed 45-min reach bake.
models.coverage: Korea — any origin where a GTFS + OSM network is built (Seoul metro first; national as feeds allow).
models.cal_method: exact routing (RAPTOR + shortest path) — no calibration constants; verified against known point-to-point journey times.
models.calibration: n/a (exact); honesty check = spot journeys vs published trip times (e.g. Seoul Stn → Gangnam).
models.sources: Korea GTFS (subway + bus timetables) · OSM Korea (walk/road network) · origin point (user-picked).
models.standard: RAPTOR (Delling et al.) for transit + Dijkstra/CH for street legs; isochrone surface via grid interpolation / alpha-shapes.
models.data_status: BUILT for Seoul: door-to-door NETWORK travel time from any of 471 stations (33 km/h + 0.5-min dwell; Seoul Station origin baked). Not yet timetable-exact RAPTOR — that's the key-gated GTFS upgrade.
models.provider: reproducible script — networkx Dijkstra over live OSM (keyless)
models.data_in: Origin point + departure time · Korea GTFS timetables · OSM walk/road network · destination zones.
models.data_out: Minutes from the origin to all 471 stations + travel-time bands — VIEWABLE on the Outputs screen (Travel time tab).

model_steps.label: Raw sources
model_steps.inputs: Published federal/open files (keyless bulk): LODES8 WAC/RAC blocks, PL-94-171 households, ACS B08301, OSM, GTFS
model_steps.outputs: Verbatim raw tables, cached with vintage + source URL
model_steps.why: Keyless bulk downloads make every input re-fetchable by anyone — reproducibility starts at the source.
model_steps.cons: Vintages differ across sources (2019/2020/2022); the audit records each rather than pretending one date.
model_steps.detail: The raw layer is never edited — transformations happen downstream so the source stays provable.
model_steps.alternatives: Different sources per region under the same raw-layer contract — Eurostat, national censuses, OSM extracts; swap the source row in Datasets.

model_steps.label: Block→zone crosswalk
model_steps.inputs: Raw block-level socio + zone boundary polygons (TAZ/tract/BG/hex/custom)
model_steps.outputs: Zone-level workers/jobs/households tables for the chosen shape
model_steps.why: One validated crosswalk decouples data from shape — swap the zone system without touching the sources.
model_steps.cons: Areal allocation error where blocks straddle zone edges (measured: workers per-zone median 0.93, households 0.99 vs CTPS).
model_steps.alternatives: Areal weighting ↔ worker-weighted allocation ↔ dasymetric (land-use masked); the crosswalk step is explicitly swappable.

model_steps.label: Census inputs
model_steps.detail: Worker + resident counts (LODES WAC/RAC), commute-mode targets (ACS B08301), households (Decennial PL-94-171) and the road network (OSM highways) are assembled into zone tables. This is the model's input layer — swap a dataset row here and every downstream step re-derives.
model_steps.inputs: Zone tables: workers, jobs, households per zone (from the block→zone crosswalk)
model_steps.outputs: Per-zone productions/attractions basis
model_steps.why: Census-anchored zones decouple socio data from any one zone system — the same inputs run on TAZ, tract, block group or a custom shape.
model_steps.cons: Block-level socio is top-down disaggregated where not published; per-zone error grows as zones shrink.
model_steps.alternatives: Swap the ZONE SYSTEM entirely (Zones tab): TAZ ↔ tract ↔ block group ↔ hex ↔ custom polygon — same inputs, different shape.

model_steps.label: Trip Generation
model_steps.detail: Turns land use + workers into trip productions (P_i) and attractions (A_j) per zone using cross-classification rates. Editable middle step: swap the rate table or the classification method without touching the steps around it.
model_steps.outputs: P_i: HBW productions per zone
model_steps.why: Workers×rate is the standard, defensible HBW generator (NCHRP-716).
model_steps.cons: Home-based-work only today — non-work and time-of-day trips are not yet modeled.
model_steps.alternatives: Workers × rate ↔ cross-classification ↔ regression trip rates.
model_steps.math: P_i = workers_i x rate · A_j = jobs_j x rate (productions/attractions)

model_steps.label: Trip Distribution
model_steps.detail: Pairs productions with attractions into an origin-destination matrix via a gravity model whose impedance parameter beta is calibrated to observed trip length (NHTS 2017). Interchangeable: beta is a single tunable row — raise it and trips stay local, lower it and they spread.
model_steps.outputs: OD matrix (gravity, IPF-balanced)
model_steps.why: Gravity with calibrated β reproduces observed trip lengths with one interpretable knob.
model_steps.cons: β can hit its floor on compact geographies — trip length becomes geometry-limited (shown as an honest warn in the audit).
model_steps.alternatives: Gravity + IPF ↔ destination-choice logit ↔ intervening opportunities.
model_steps.math: T_ij = P_i · A_j · f(c_ij), f = exp(-beta·c_ij); doubly-constrained Furness/IPF balancing to P and A

model_steps.label: Mode Choice
model_steps.detail: Splits each OD flow across car / transit / walk with a multinomial logit whose transit constant (transit_calib) is calibrated to the observed ACS mode share. This is the interchangeable heart of the chain — swap the utility spec or the calibration constant and only this bubble changes.
model_steps.inputs: OD matrix + transit utility + calibrated transit share
model_steps.outputs: Mode-split OD (transit vs car)
model_steps.why: Share×calibration hits the observed ACS transit share exactly where sourced local targets exist.
model_steps.cons: A share model, not full nested logit — no income/vehicle segmentation within a zone yet.
model_steps.alternatives: Share × calibration ↔ binary / nested logit (needs income + vehicle segmentation data).
model_steps.math: share_ij = clamp(share_town x transit_calib, 0, max_share); logit option: P(transit) = e^U / sum e^U

model_steps.label: Trip Assignment
model_steps.detail: Loads the mode-split OD matrix onto the OSM road + transit network, producing link volumes, volume/capacity ratios and corridor loads. Swap the assignment algorithm (all-or-nothing vs. equilibrium) as its own row.
model_steps.outputs: Link flows, V/C, speeds per corridor
model_steps.why: Per-corridor BPR assignment exposes where demand meets capacity.
model_steps.cons: Static assignment, no equilibrium iteration or peak spreading yet.
model_steps.alternatives: Static BPR ↔ user-equilibrium ↔ stochastic assignment.
model_steps.math: corridor V/C; BPR congested time t = t0 · (1 + alpha·(V/C)^beta_bpr)

model_steps.label: Scenario summary
model_steps.detail: The published outputs: transit share %, VMT, average trip length and the loaded corridors — the numbers that flow into the cockpit dashboards and carry a run_id + confidence tier for the reproducibility trace.
model_steps.outputs: transit %, trips, VMT, V/C, $/mi per segment, per-year 2010–2050
model_steps.why: One summary per run, pinned to a model version, so every number is traceable.
model_steps.cons: Forecast years inherit the base-year calibration — behavior change beyond growth factors is not modeled.
model_steps.alternatives: The summary set is composable — add or remove metrics via the Metric families registry.

model_steps.label: Cost-benefit accounting
model_steps.method: BCA from the per-scenario flow block; value_of_time $18/hr, wage_value $150/work-trip — coefficients labeled ILLUSTRATIVE in config/model.json
model_steps.inputs: scenario summaries: trips, person-hours, vehicle flow, V/C, realized mph
model_steps.outputs: benefit/cost per day and per year, B/C ratio, value_transacted_usd
model_steps.why: turns model flows into comparable dollars across scenarios
model_steps.cons: coefficients are illustrative, not locally estimated; no incidence detail
model_steps.alternatives: full FTA-guidance CBA ↔ per-corridor benefit incidence
model_steps.math: cost-benefit with BOTH lenses: wealth-neutral (every hour equal) vs wage-weighted, side by side

model_steps.label: Soundness audit
model_steps.method: soundness_report.py: report_parses, zones/trips positive, share in bounds, share + trip-length within tolerance, trips_monotonic, mass_sanity, foundation_provenance, targets_sourced, calibration_mode_noted — plus tier stamp
model_steps.inputs: run report + foundation provenance block + sourced targets
model_steps.outputs: pass/warn/fail per check, summary counts, confidence-tier stamp
model_steps.why: every run self-audits before its numbers are trusted
model_steps.cons: checks tolerance and provenance, not ground truth
model_steps.alternatives: manual peer review ↔ STOPS-style validation suite

model_steps.label: Calibration
model_steps.sublabel: solves β + transit_calib to targets — method selectable
model_steps.detail: The calibration loop as its own interchangeable component: it solves the model's knobs (β, transit_calib) against observed targets (NHTS trip length, ACS transit share). Which ALGORITHM does the solving is a per-run selection on the Run setup card — bisection today; IPF balances the trip table to margins; Bayesian optimization searches several knobs jointly. The chosen method is frozen onto every run's snapshot.
model_steps.inputs: Observed targets (NHTS 2017 trip length, ACS B08301 share) + model outputs per trial
model_steps.outputs: Solved knobs: β → Trip Distribution, transit_calib → Mode Choice; method + residuals stamped on the run
model_steps.why: Making the solver a swappable row keeps calibration honest and modular — swap the algorithm without touching the steps around it.
model_steps.cons: Each method has its own must-document clause (see Methods registry); Bayes-opt is server-only — the loop re-runs the model each trial.
model_steps.alternatives: Bisection (one knob per target) ↔ IPF / Furness (table balancing to margins) ↔ Bayesian optimization (multi-parameter search, server-side).
model_steps.math: bisection (or secant): beta -> observed mean trip mi; transit_calib -> observed transit share

model_steps.label: Census series
model_steps.inputs: PEP county components v2019; LODES MA WAC 2011/2015/2019; 2019 cousub gazetteer
model_steps.outputs: raw county series, gitignored, fetch commands in the module docstring
model_steps.why: observed history is the only basis — no borrowed growth assumptions
model_steps.alternatives: hold anchor-year inputs only (no forecast)
model_steps.cons: window starts 2015 — pre-COVID momentum; post-2020 vintages re-fit in one command

model_steps.label: Fit rates
model_steps.method: per-capita components + per-sector shift-share vs MA
model_steps.outputs: birth/death/net-migration rates; state sector growth + county regional shift
model_steps.why: recent window = current momentum; the reference economy anchors sector trends
model_steps.alternatives: full cohort-component tables; Bayesian rate priors
model_steps.cons: constant recent-window rates — no age-structured fertility/mortality yet
model_steps.math: b,d,m = mean(B,D,M)/P over 2015-2019; g_s = (E_s19/E_s15)^(1/4) - 1; r_cs = a_cs - g_s

model_steps.label: Project 2020-2050
model_steps.outputs: county population + jobs totals per horizon year
model_steps.why: local advantages fade toward the reference — never runaway extrapolation
model_steps.alternatives: sub-county allocation from permits/land capacity
model_steps.cons: uniform-within-county town allocation (the honest floor)
model_steps.math: P(y+1) = P(y)·(1+b-d+m), clamp ±2%/yr; E_cs(y+1) = E_cs(y)·(1+g_s+r_cs·0.5^(dy/10)), clamp ±4%/yr

model_steps.label: Back-cast check
model_steps.outputs: published skill block (per-county + region)
model_steps.why: forecast skill is MEASURED, not asserted — the score ships with the data
model_steps.alternatives: historic GTFS to 2009 as a service-side truth check
model_steps.cons: 2011 is one hindcast target; more vintages = stronger skill curve
model_steps.math: same operators inverted to 2011; APE_c = |pred-obs|/obs; MAPE published

model_steps.label: forecast_totals.json
model_steps.method: town factors vs anchor via county join
model_steps.outputs: per-town worker/job factors + method + provenance + confidence + skill
model_steps.why: the engine consumes factors ONLY behind forecast:true — defaults byte-identical
model_steps.alternatives: adopt agency projections where an MPO publishes better
model_steps.cons: exploratory tier — labeled on every surface it reaches

model_steps.label: Static GTFS
model_steps.outputs: raw timetables (out-of-git, one-command refetch)
model_steps.why: exact timetables beat average-wait constants
model_steps.alternatives: live A7 daily index on the box (already running for departures)
model_steps.cons: one feed vintage per bake; rating-period changes need a refetch

model_steps.label: Service day + patterns
model_steps.method: busiest-weekday auto-pick (RAPTOR_DATE override); trips grouped by identical stop sequence
model_steps.outputs: routable pattern set + footpaths (transfers.txt + ≤300m pairs)
model_steps.why: patterns scan once per round — the speed that makes exactness affordable
model_steps.alternatives: explicit RAPTOR_DATE per bake
model_steps.cons: busiest-weekday pick is a heuristic (announced, overridable)

model_steps.label: RAPTOR rounds
model_steps.outputs: exact arrival at every stop + parent pointers for legs
model_steps.why: 15 fixture checks vs hand-computed optima; honest: a 16-second late walk misses the trip
model_steps.alternatives: compiled port when the agent rung needs it
model_steps.cons: pure Python — fast enough for bakes, not per-agent loops yet
model_steps.math: round k: tau_k(stop) = earliest arrival using <= k transit legs; per-pattern earliest-catchable-trip scan; footpath relaxation between rounds

model_steps.label: 45-min reach bake
model_steps.method: per-zone RAPTOR @ 08:00 weekday; walk ≤1km / P&R ≤6km access
model_steps.outputs: boston_transit_reach.json — the seam the engine already reads
model_steps.why: replaced the straight-line proxy: 2019 jobs≤45min 837k → 268k, access_method states the basis
model_steps.alternatives: frequency-blended multi-departure bake
model_steps.cons: one departure time (08:00) per bake — timetable-honest, time-sensitive

model_steps.label: Journey planner
model_steps.outputs: walk/ride legs with routes, board/alight stops + times
model_steps.why: the F1 primitive — the departures applet grows into this; agents inherit it later
model_steps.alternatives: door-to-door applet wiring (F1) exposes real choices
model_steps.cons: walk/P&R access constants shared with the skim — documented, editable

model_steps.label: Four-step engine
model_steps.method: compiled model core; zones cached per year; forecast factors opt-in
model_steps.math: the four subprocess steps run in sequence over the zone vectors; all matrix ops vectorized
model_steps.inputs: zone workers/jobs vectors (+growth levers, +forecast factors when opted in), shares, params (beta, calib)
model_steps.outputs: trip matrices, per-town rollups, corridors, summary
model_steps.why: one warm process = ~1s scenarios; the same engine serves HTTP, worker mode, and the compiled binary
model_steps.cons: single-region per call; equilibrium assignment still first-order
model_steps.alternatives: compiled binary (PackageCompiler); future equilibrium loop (D9)

model_steps.label: Intermediate processing
model_steps.inputs: Raw block/point observations from the sources step.
model_steps.outputs: Model-ready zone values that are smooth where the data is thin and sharp where real barriers cut (rail, water, highways).
model_steps.why: Published census grain (tract/block-group) is coarse and noisy for small areas; raw points are spiky. The averaging+smoothing pair gives honest sub-tract detail without inventing people.
model_steps.cons: Every derived layer must carry its method + parameters, or a smoothed number reads as observed. Documented, never silent.
model_steps.alternatives: Skip it (use published grain as-is) · dasymetric only · radius/KDE only · pycnophylactic only — each a swappable module.

model_steps.label: Input data
model_steps.inputs: LODES/ACS/decennial at block · OSM features · GTFS stops.
model_steps.outputs: Aligned raw layers keyed to geometry.
model_steps.why: The averaging/smoothing pair needs the raw layers aligned to one geometry first.
model_steps.cons: Misaligned keys silently drop rows; alignment is validated.
model_steps.alternatives: Which layers to include — swappable.

model_steps.label: Geo averaging
model_steps.inputs: Raw layers + a land-use / population mask.
model_steps.outputs: Ambient values (what is near here) and mass reallocated onto inhabited land.
model_steps.why: Access variables answer 'what is within reach'; radius/KDE captures that. Stock variables (people, jobs) get dasymetrically reallocated so density lands where people actually live.
model_steps.cons: Radius false-seeds empty gaps between separated neighborhoods unless paired with a mask; the rule is stock→dasymetric, ambient→radius.
model_steps.alternatives: Kernel bandwidth choice · dasymetric mask source (NLCD vs buildings) — swappable.

model_steps.label: Geo smoothing
model_steps.inputs: Averaged surface + a barrier mask (rail / water / limited-access roads).
model_steps.outputs: A smooth surface that PRESERVES each zone's total and does NOT bleed across real barriers.
model_steps.why: Tobler pycnophylactic interpolation removes tract-edge cliffs while conserving mass; barrier-aware masking keeps the smoothing from crossing a rail line or river that people can't.
model_steps.cons: Smooths genuine cliffs unless the barrier mask is supplied; conservation must be checked (each zone sum = 1.000).
model_steps.alternatives: Iteration count · barrier set · plain vs barrier-aware — swappable.

model_steps.label: Output data
model_steps.outputs: Model-ready inputs handed to the block→zone crosswalk and downstream models.
model_steps.why: A clean hand-off row makes the boundary between processed data and the model explicit and auditable.
model_steps.cons: If skipped, provenance of what fed the model gets fuzzy.
model_steps.alternatives: Emit to crosswalk vs straight to model — swappable.

model_steps.label: Korea transit feed
model_steps.inputs: data.go.kr TAGO / Seoul Open Data / GTFS mirror — stations, bus stops, route segments.
model_steps.outputs: Stops (nodes) + route segments (edges) + transfer candidates.
model_steps.why: Centrality is only as honest as the network it reads; the feed defines which stops and connections exist.
model_steps.cons: Feed coverage gaps bias the ranking; stated per run.
model_steps.alternatives: data.go.kr TAGO vs Seoul Open Data vs GTFS mirror — swappable source.

model_steps.label: Build network graph
model_steps.inputs: Stops + route segments + OSM walkable transfers.
model_steps.outputs: A weighted transit graph (optionally travel-time or headway weighted).
model_steps.why: Centrality is a property of the graph; the honest step is HOW stops connect (same platform, walkable transfer, route adjacency).
model_steps.cons: Transfer radius + directedness are choices that change results; documented per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Undirected vs directed · unweighted vs time-weighted · transfer radius — swappable.

model_steps.label: Compute centralities
model_steps.outputs: Four centrality scores per stop.
model_steps.why: Each measure answers a different 'important how' — bridge (betweenness), hub (degree), central (closeness), influential (PageRank).
model_steps.cons: Exact betweenness is O(VE); large national graphs need approximation (sampled sources).
model_steps.alternatives: Exact vs sampled betweenness · eigenvector vs PageRank — swappable.

model_steps.label: Ranked hubs + map
model_steps.outputs: Ranked hub list + point/heat map of structural importance.
model_steps.why: A ranked hub list + map is the decision-ready artifact planners use.
model_steps.cons: A single measure can mislead; publish all four and the method.
model_steps.alternatives: Rank by betweenness vs PageRank vs composite — swappable.

model_steps.label: Origin + time
model_steps.sublabel: where you start · when you leave
model_steps.inputs: A picked origin (lat/lon or stop) + departure datetime + mode set.
model_steps.outputs: A routing query.
model_steps.why: Everything downstream is from HERE at THIS time — the query names both.
model_steps.cons: One minute is a snapshot; a window is more robust.
model_steps.alternatives: Single time vs departure window — swappable.

model_steps.label: Build multimodal network
model_steps.outputs: A time-expanded transit graph + street network for access/egress legs.
model_steps.why: Door-to-door time = walk to stop + wait + ride + transfers + walk from stop; needs both layers stitched.
model_steps.cons: Walk speed + max-transfer + max-walk are parameters that shift the surface; documented per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Walk speed · transfer limit · include bikeshare — swappable.

model_steps.label: Route to all zones
model_steps.math: earliest-arrival per round; τ(z)=min over stops (arrival + egress walk)
model_steps.outputs: Earliest arrival time to every destination zone.
model_steps.why: RAPTOR gives timetable-EXACT earliest arrivals with bounded transfers — the same proven engine as the router, aimed from one origin.
model_steps.cons: One departure minute is one snapshot; a robust surface averages a departure window.
model_steps.alternatives: Single departure vs profile (window average) — swappable.

model_steps.label: Interpolate surface
model_steps.outputs: A smooth travel-time surface + isochrone bands.
model_steps.why: Point times read as a heat map only after honest interpolation; bands make 'within 30 min' legible.
model_steps.cons: Interpolation between sparse reachable points can over-smooth across un-served gaps; bands clip to reachable zones.
model_steps.alternatives: IDW vs kriging vs alpha-shape bands — swappable.

model_steps.label: Travel-time heat map
model_steps.outputs: An interactive heat map of estimated travel time from the chosen origin across Korea.
model_steps.why: The heat map is the answer a planner reads — where you can get to, and how fast.
model_steps.cons: Interpolation can imply reachability across un-served gaps; bands clip to reachable zones.
model_steps.alternatives: IDW vs kriging vs alpha-shape bands — swappable.

model_steps.label: Network inputs
model_steps.inputs: Korea GTFS timetables (stops/routes/trips/stop_times) + OSM street network.
model_steps.outputs: Transit + street layers aligned to one geometry.
model_steps.why: Door-to-door time needs the timetable layer and the walk/road layer stitched to a shared geometry before routing.
model_steps.cons: Misaligned stop-to-street snapping silently drops access legs; tolerance is validated.
model_steps.alternatives: Which GTFS feed + which OSM extract — swappable.

model_steps.label: Time-expand transit
model_steps.outputs: A time-expanded transit graph (arrival/departure events as timed nodes).
model_steps.why: RAPTOR needs timetable events, not average headways — time-expansion preserves exact catchable trips.
model_steps.cons: Node count grows with service span and frequency.
model_steps.alternatives: Time-expanded vs time-dependent vs frequency graph — swappable.

model_steps.label: Stitch street layer
model_steps.inputs: OSM streets + stop locations + walk-speed / max-walk params.
model_steps.outputs: Access/egress walk legs + max-walk transfer footpaths linking stops into the graph.
model_steps.why: Origins/destinations are rarely at a stop; the street layer supplies first/last-leg and transfer walks.
model_steps.cons: Walk speed, max-walk and max-transfer shift every downstream time; documented per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Walk speed · max-walk radius · include bikeshare — swappable.

model_steps.label: Multimodal graph
model_steps.outputs: One routable multimodal network handed to the RAPTOR routing step.
model_steps.why: An explicit hand-off makes which network produced a surface auditable.
model_steps.cons: If skipped, the network version behind a surface is unclear.
model_steps.alternatives: Emit combined graph vs separate transit/street graphs — swappable.

model_steps.label: Stops + segments in
model_steps.inputs: Stops (from the feed) + route segments + OSM walkable transfer candidates.
model_steps.outputs: Aligned node set + candidate edge set keyed to geometry.
model_steps.why: The graph is only as honest as the stops and connections it starts from; align them first.
model_steps.cons: Feed coverage gaps drop nodes; gaps stated per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Transfer-candidate source (OSM vs feed transfers.txt) — swappable.

model_steps.label: Nodes = stops
model_steps.outputs: Graph nodes with same-platform/same-station stops merged.
model_steps.why: Whether two platforms are one node or two changes every centrality score; the merge rule is the honest choice.
model_steps.cons: Over-merging hides interchange penalty; under-merging inflates degree. Documented per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Merge by station id vs radius vs none — swappable.

model_steps.label: Edges = segments + transfers
model_steps.inputs: Merged nodes + route segments + transfer candidates + weighting params.
model_steps.outputs: Weighted edges (route-adjacent + walkable transfers), directed or undirected.
model_steps.why: Centrality is a property of HOW stops connect; edge rules define the graph.
model_steps.cons: Transfer radius and directedness change results; documented per run.
model_steps.alternatives: Undirected vs directed · unweighted vs time/headway-weighted · transfer radius — swappable.

model_steps.label: Weighted graph
model_steps.outputs: One weighted transit graph handed to the centrality step.
model_steps.why: An explicit graph hand-off makes the exact graph a run scored auditable.
model_steps.cons: If skipped, which graph variant produced a ranking is unclear.
model_steps.alternatives: Emit one graph vs per-mode subgraphs — swappable.

wellbeing_factors.basis: CNT Housing + Transportation (H+T) Affordability Index — true affordability = housing PLUS transport as % of income; >45% combined = burdened. Established planning standard.
wellbeing_factors.why: Cheap rent with a forced expensive car is not affordable — H+T is the honest cost of living somewhere.
wellbeing_factors.cons: Transport cost is modeled, not observed per household.

wellbeing_factors.basis: United Way ALICE threshold (Asset-Limited, Income-Constrained, Employed) + MIT Living Wage Calculator — the measured line between surviving and drowning for working households.
wellbeing_factors.source: ACS income vs county living-wage basket (MIT LWC)
wellbeing_factors.why: Median income hides the households just under the survival line — ALICE counts them explicitly.
wellbeing_factors.cons: Basket costs update yearly; county grain coarser than tract.

wellbeing_factors.basis: Chetty et al. Social Capital Atlas (2022) — economic connectedness is among the strongest predictors of upward mobility ever measured; Putnam's social-capital research frames the decline.
wellbeing_factors.why: Whether a place makes it easy to meet people is measurable — connectedness, civic organizations, gathering places.
wellbeing_factors.cons: Atlas built from Facebook ties (one platform, one era); third places are a proxy for use, not use itself.

wellbeing_factors.basis: OECD Better Life Index (work-life balance dimension) + American Time Use Survey; 'time poverty' research shows discretionary time predicts wellbeing independent of income.
wellbeing_factors.source: ATUS + ACS commute time (B08303) + free-venue density (parks, libraries)
wellbeing_factors.why: A long commute plus pay-to-exist leisure is a wellbeing tax — free time that costs nothing is the asset.
wellbeing_factors.cons: ATUS is a national sample — small-area values are modeled (small-area estimation, documented).

wellbeing_factors.basis: Trust for Public Land ParkServe (10-minute-walk park access standard) + Oldenburg's third-place research.
wellbeing_factors.why: Living life outside the home without a fee is a place property, not a personality trait.
wellbeing_factors.cons: Quality/safety of a space is harder than its presence; needs local input.

wellbeing_factors.basis: CDC PLACES (tract-level modeled health outcomes) + HRSA Health Professional Shortage Areas — the federal standards for local health measurement.
wellbeing_factors.source: CDC PLACES + HRSA HPSA + CMS facility locations
wellbeing_factors.why: Care deserts and outcome gaps are the hard floor under every other wellbeing factor.
wellbeing_factors.cons: PLACES values are model-based small-area estimates — carry their published confidence intervals.

wellbeing_factors.basis: NHTSA FARS (every fatal crash, geocoded, public) — the standard for traffic-safety analysis.
wellbeing_factors.source: FARS + local crash open data where published
wellbeing_factors.why: Traffic violence is a leading, mappable, preventable harm — and car-dependence multiplies exposure.
wellbeing_factors.cons: Non-fatal crash data is uneven across states.

wellbeing_factors.basis: ARDA U.S. Religion Census (county congregations & adherents) — the standing academic source; included as optional per design (not main, worth adding).
wellbeing_factors.why: For many people congregation IS the social fabric; optional weight respects that it is not universal.

wellbeing_factors.basis: NCES school/college locations + Chetty Opportunity Atlas (neighborhood effects on children's outcomes).
wellbeing_factors.why: Distance and cost to education is a livability gate for households with kids — and shapes who can live where.
wellbeing_factors.cons: School quality measures are contested; access ≠ admission.

methods.purpose: Redistribute tract/BG values onto land where people actually live (pseudo-block granularity).
methods.when_use: Stock variables (people, households, income) needing finer-than-published grain.
methods.approach: Mask zone values with ancillary land use (NLCD/buildings), reallocate proportionally.
methods.cons: Only as good as the mask; never invents beyond the zone total.
methods.documentation: Mask source + vintage + reallocation weights logged on every derived layer.

methods.purpose: Melt adjacent tracts into a smooth surface that PRESERVES totals (Tobler 1979).
methods.when_use: The 'melting tracts' path — gradual surfaces without inventing people.
methods.approach: Iterative smoothing constrained so each zone's mass is conserved.
methods.cons: Smooths real cliffs (tracks, highways) unless barrier-aware masking is added.
methods.documentation: Iterations, barrier mask, and conservation check (must equal 1.000) logged.

methods.purpose: The radius-based rolling average merged to the map — tunable level of detail.
methods.when_use: Ambient access variables (amenities, services) where 'what is near me' is the question.
methods.approach: Kernel density / moving-window mean with a chosen radius (bandwidth).
methods.cons: False-seeds empty gaps between separated neighborhoods unless paired with a dasymetric mask.
methods.documentation: Kernel type + radius + mask logged on the layer; radius shown in the legend.

methods.purpose: The decision rule between the two granularity paths.
methods.when_use: Always, before deriving any sub-tract layer.
methods.approach: Stock variables (people, homes, income) → dasymetric + pycnophylactic (totals preserved). Ambient access → radius/KDE. Never radius-smooth a stock variable.
methods.cons: Mixed variables (jobs) may justify both — then publish both with labels.
methods.documentation: The chosen path + why, stamped on the layer row.

methods.purpose: Model tract/block values where the survey does not publish them.
methods.when_use: ATUS-style national samples needed locally; PLACES already does this for health.
methods.approach: Regression/synthetic estimation from covariates; publish variance.
methods.cons: Model-based — must never be presented as observed.
methods.documentation: Model form, covariates, and confidence intervals published with the layer.

methods.purpose: Combine factors into one score without hiding judgment calls.
methods.when_use: The wellbeing index; any composite.
methods.approach: Median-first for skewed money variables (median vs mean shown side by side); z-score or min-max normalize; weights are EXPLICIT rows users adjust.
methods.cons: Weights are value judgments — the honest fix is publishing them, not hiding them.
methods.documentation: Normalization + weights + median/mean choice stored as rows beside the score.

methods.purpose: Differences across ethnicity, nationality, education, industry, car access, kids, spouse…
methods.when_use: Any 'compare groups' question.
methods.approach: ACS PUMS microdata cross-tabulation with published margins of error.
methods.cons: Small cells get suppressed/noisy — show MOE, never a bare point estimate.
methods.documentation: Universe, cells suppressed, and margins of error carried with every split.

methods.purpose: Solve model knobs (β, transit share) against observed targets.
methods.when_use: Every city calibration (proven on 382 metros).
methods.approach: Bisection on the residual until within tolerance.
methods.cons: One knob per target; multi-objective needs care.
methods.documentation: Target source + vintage + residual logged per run (audit checks 5-6).

methods.purpose: Balance a trip/OD table one margin at a time until every control total matches.
methods.when_use: Trip-table balancing to known row/column targets (the STOPS-style move); distribution matrices after gravity.
methods.approach: Scale rows to row targets, then columns to column targets, cycle until converged. Aliases: Furness (transport), RAS/biproportional (economics), raking (surveys). Deterministic — no search.
methods.cons: Needs consistent margins and a feasible seed matrix — structural zeros stay zero; cannot tune model parameters, only tables.
methods.documentation: Margin sources + vintages, seed-matrix provenance, convergence tolerance + iteration count logged per application.
methods.package: server: ProportionalFitting.jl (MIT) · device: ~30-line engine function (no dependency)

methods.purpose: Tune several expensive model parameters jointly against observed targets in few trials.
methods.when_use: Multi-parameter calibration where each trial is a full model run (β + transit_calib + growth jointly); when bisection's one-knob-per-target no longer fits.
methods.approach: Gaussian-process surrogate fitted to past trials; an acquisition function (expected improvement) picks the next most-informative setting; evaluate, update, repeat.
methods.cons: Stochastic — irreproducible without a pinned seed; overkill for one knob (bisection wins there); runs must live beside the model (server).
methods.documentation: Objective + target sources, parameter bounds/priors, trial count, random seed, surrogate + acquisition kind logged per calibration.
methods.package: server: BayesianOptimization.jl / Surrogates.jl (MIT) — loop co-located with the Julia model on forge

methods.purpose: Move census-block data onto any zone system with totals preserved.
methods.when_use: Every zone-system change (TAZ / BG / tract / hex / custom).
methods.approach: Area/centroid apportionment through one validated crosswalk; conversion validated per system (medians 0.93–0.99, see Zones).
methods.cons: Validation varies by variable — jobs spread wider than households.
methods.documentation: Crosswalk build + per-system validation medians stamped on the zone_systems row.

methods.purpose: Turn zone socio counts into trip productions and attractions.
methods.when_use: Trip generation from census workers/households (FHWA practice).
methods.approach: Category rate table × zone counts → P_i / A_j vectors.
methods.cons: Rates are transferable averages — local survey rates beat them where available.
methods.documentation: Rate table source + vintage logged per run.
methods.package: built into the Julia four-step engine (forge)

methods.purpose: Pair productions with attractions by size and travel impedance.
methods.when_use: OD distribution when only aggregate flows are observed.
methods.approach: T_ij ∝ P_i·A_j·f(c_ij) with calibrated impedance β; balanced to margins (IPF).
methods.cons: β can hit its floor on compact geographies — trip length becomes geometry-limited (honest audit warn).
methods.documentation: β value + calibration target + friction form logged per run.
methods.package: built into the Julia four-step engine (forge)

methods.purpose: Split each OD flow across modes by relative utility.
methods.when_use: Mode shares from times/costs + a calibrated constant (NCHRP-716 / STOPS).
methods.approach: P(mode)=e^V/Σe^V; transit constant calibrated to the observed ACS share.
methods.cons: IIA assumption; no income/vehicle segmentation within a zone yet.
methods.documentation: Utility spec + constants + target-share source logged per run.
methods.package: built into the Julia four-step engine (forge)

methods.purpose: Load the mode-split OD onto the network — volumes, speeds, V/C.
methods.when_use: Corridor loads and congestion from an OD matrix.
methods.approach: Shortest-path loading with capacity feedback (all-or-nothing ↔ equilibrium, swappable).
methods.cons: Static assignment — no peak spreading or queuing dynamics.
methods.documentation: Assignment variant + network vintage logged per run.
methods.package: built into the Julia four-step engine (forge)

methods.purpose: Monetize scenario flow deltas into benefit-cost figures.
methods.when_use: Comparing scenarios in money terms.
methods.approach: Published coefficients × flow deltas (time, wage) — coefficients labeled ILLUSTRATIVE.
methods.cons: Results scale linearly with coefficient choices — publish them, never bury them.
methods.documentation: Coefficient set + ILLUSTRATIVE labels carried on every report.

methods.purpose: Turn stops + routes + transfers into a graph a network algorithm can read.
methods.when_use: Any centrality / routing model over a transit network.
methods.approach: Nodes = stops/stations; edges = consecutive route segments + walkable transfers (within a radius); optional weights = travel time or headway.
methods.cons: Directedness, transfer radius and weighting all change downstream results — must be logged.
methods.documentation: Transfer radius, directed/undirected, edge weight, and feed vintage stamped on every derived layer.

methods.purpose: Rank nodes by structural importance in a graph.
methods.when_use: Finding critical hubs / connectivity / accessibility in a transit network.
methods.approach: Degree (connections), betweenness (Brandes — how many shortest paths pass through), closeness (mean distance to all), PageRank/eigenvector (importance weighted by neighbours).
methods.cons: Exact betweenness is O(VE); approximate with sampled sources on national graphs; each measure means a DIFFERENT 'important'.
methods.documentation: Which measures, exact vs sampled, and normalization published with the ranking.

methods.purpose: Turn per-origin routed times into a smooth, banded heat map.
methods.when_use: Where-can-I-get-to-from-here questions; access equity mapping.
methods.approach: Route from one origin to all zones (RAPTOR + street legs), then interpolate the point times to a surface and cut isochrone bands (15/30/45/60 min).
methods.cons: Interpolation can bridge un-served gaps; clip bands to actually-reachable zones and state the departure time.
methods.documentation: Departure time (or window), interpolation method, and band edges published with the map.

methods.purpose: Timetable-exact earliest-arrival journeys over static GTFS.
methods.when_use: Any transit travel-time, accessibility, or journey-planning need.
methods.approach: Round-based Round-bAsed Public Transit Optimized Router (Delling et al.): each round relaxes one more transfer, scanning trip patterns; service-date aware; footpaths for transfers.
methods.cons: One departure minute is a snapshot; profile routing over a window is heavier; static timetable ≠ real-time delays.
methods.documentation: Feed vintage, service date, max transfers, and departure time stamped on every routed output.

methods.purpose: Machine-translate text pre-pass (a HuggingFace model, not a formula).
methods.when_use: Any pipeline stage that needs source text translated before downstream processing.
methods.cons: Network model — quality/latency depend on the served checkpoint; not deterministic math like the registry's other entries.
methods.documentation: hf_repo + revision, provider id, and intent stamped wherever this method is selected. It is a model, not a formula — approach is intentionally empty.

methods.purpose: Turn text into a fixed-length embedding vector for downstream similarity/search.
methods.when_use: Any pipeline stage needing a text embedding (e.g. algarec-style recommendation hops).
methods.cons: Network model — served vector quality depends on the checkpoint; not deterministic math like the registry's other entries.
methods.documentation: hf_repo + revision, provider id, and intent stamped wherever this method is selected. It is a model, not a formula — approach is intentionally empty.
